question: A 12-year-old got past our age gate and has been using Murshid for a month without a parent's consent. What do UAE rules require us to do now, and what do other countries require?
answer: UAE: Federal Decree-Law No. 26 of 2025 (Child Digital Safety) Article (7) requires verifiable parental consent for processing data of children under 13 [uae-child-digital-safety-2025#0009]. The platform must also provide a mechanism for withdrawing consent, disclose privacy policies, and restrict data access. However, Article (8) provides an exemption for educational platforms if they meet safety measures and obtain Cabinet approval [uae-child-digital-safety-2025#0010]. Since the child is 12 and used the service without consent, the school/platform must stop processing the child's data, obtain verifiable parental consent retroactively, and implement the documented consent and withdrawal mechanisms. Global: The UK Age Appropriate Design Code (ICO) mirrors this, stating that processing a child's data under 13 is lawful only with parental consent [uk-age-appropriate-design-code#0166]. UNESCO (2023) notes that general-purpose AI like ChatGPT requires users to be 13+, and those under 18 need parent/guardian permission, tracing to the US COPPA law [unesco-genai-education-2023#0068]. UNICEF (2025) warns that digital consent at 13 does not mean children are treated as adults [unicef-ai-children-v3-2025#0012].
gaps: The excerpts do not specify the exact penalties or enforcement steps UAE authorities will impose on the school/platform for the prior month of non-consent use, nor do they detail the procedural timeline for parental consent withdrawal or data deletion requirements beyond the general 'rapid and continuously accessible' mechanism mentioned in Article (7).
